name: FluxCast
use_label: Cast a Linux desktop to your TV
one_liner: A small tray app that casts your Linux desktop to a smart TV, no cable needed.

text.why: Windows and macOS cast to a TV out of the box; on Linux a working option is hard to find. The author says they built it after nothing worked for watching movies from a Linux laptop on the TV.
text.take: The README states plainly which modes work and which do not, which is what earns the trust.
build: Casts over Miracast (WFD), DLNA or Chromecast. The tray app follows the system language, and on KDE/GNOME Wayland it captures the screen through the desktop's screen-share dialog (xdg-desktop-portal).

who.role: Linux laptop users who want to watch video or show a presentation on a TV.

start.text: Follow the install guide in the docs at fluxcast.dev, then pick your TV from the tray.

caveat: Per the README, only WFD (Miracast) is validated as release-ready; DLNA is a fallback, and Cast is experimental and did not work on the tested Samsung TV. It is tuned for wlroots-class setups such as Hyprland.

license.scope_text: Use freely. Release your source if you redistribute (copyleft).

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
